newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end quietly with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end quietly with modest gains.

text.p: Italian stocks ended with modest gains on Thursday after a lacklustre session with little interest shown after this morning's news that November CPI showed a fall to 2.6 percent, in line with expectations, pushed prices slightly higher.
Traders said the market was hoping for an official Bank of Italy discount rate cut before the end of the year but business was likely to be fairly dull until this happened.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.56 percent up at 10,537 after a high of 10,557 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.61 percent up at 15,755 after a peak at 15,792.
Fiat performed well, ending 2.48 percent higher at 4,540 lire on continuing hopes for incentives to boost the depressed domestic car market.
Pirelli & C holding put on 3.36 percent to 1,971 lire on talk of group streamlining but energy giant ENI ended 0.15 percent off at 7,870.
Olivetti rose 4.53 percent to 534.8 while the De Benedetti financial holding Cofide put on 6.66 percent to 799.5 and the Cir financial holding rose 5.53 percent to 889.1.
Banks were generally firmer, with interest shown for Ambroveneto, Credito Italiano,Mediobanca and IMI.
Traded volume was estimated in line with the previous session at around 550 billion lire.
Telecoms were all firmer but insurances were mixed with Alleanza up 1.93 percent at 11,851 lire but INA slipped 0.05 percent to 2,074.
Agro-industrial group Montedison eased against the trend, closing 1.04 percent off at 1,050. Food group Parmalat was also weaker, off 0.86 percent at 2,421.
Traders said the recent ups and downs of the market which seems unable to take a concrete direction appeared to mean "we'll not see much happening from now to the year end."
